value.subtitle: A travel planner that composes an itinerary from two answers — a place, a duration — then hands it back as a notebook, not a booking engine.

hero.alt: Roote's world map with France selected, ready to compose
hero.caption: One country, one duration — that's the whole brief.

sections.heading: Every stop opens as a floating photograph
sections.body: Click a pin and the destination surfaces as a card, not a page: a dominant image sets the atmosphere, three lines — atmosphère, à goûter, à voir — offer to go deeper, one explicit action leads to the city itself. Underneath, a banner called "le cadre" lines up three anchors for the stay — where to sleep, the signature moment, how to reach the next stop — and keeps the count of free half-days visible the whole time. The empty time is part of the plan, not an absence of information.

facts.title: Dormir
facts.body: A neighbourhood, never a named hotel.

facts.title: Le moment signature
facts.body: One thing worth building the day around.

facts.title: Rejoindre l'étape
facts.body: How, and how long, to the next stop.

images.alt: Opening a destination card, then diving from the country map into Paris
images.caption: The zoom starts from the pin — prototype recording.

sections.heading: The map holds still so the city can move
sections.body: Inside a city, the plan pins itself to the side of the screen and stays there. Scrolling through the chapter lights up the matching landmark and recentres the legend; clicking a landmark — or a line of the legend — scrolls back to the place. Photography carries most of the argument: full colour, never cropped by a filter, never repeated twice in the same itinerary. The opening shot loads first, the rest waits its turn.

images.alt: Scrollytelling chapter for Paris with the city plan fixed on the right
images.caption: The plan repins itself to every place named in the text.

sections.heading: The photographs have their own back office
sections.body: Ten countries, roughly thirty cities: every photo needed a source, a licence and a credit, without a paid API and without becoming a second job. The curation tool reviews them one at a time, Tinder-style — confirm, reject, or pull an alternative from Wikimedia Commons, Openverse or a free Pexels key, without leaving the card. Whatever comes in — a search result, a dropped file, a pasted URL — lands at the same 1800px, JPEG quality 82, credited automatically in the codebase that ships.

facts.title: Confirmer / rejeter
facts.body: Y or N — the two outcomes that matter, one keystroke each.

facts.title: Alternatives
facts.body: Commons, Openverse or Pexels, searched from inside the card.

facts.title: Recadrage automatique
facts.body: Every image lands at 1800px, JPEG q82, credited in code.

images.alt: Curation tool in focus mode reviewing a Hong Kong hero photo
images.caption: The review pass nobody sees, run before every photo ships.

value.outro: Ten countries are traced so far, from Paris to Chongqing — the live version keeps growing most weekends.
